# bugs #2536: Error 66 for an array whose size expression (0x1P2 > 10) is zero

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2536/
- Category: [No action recommended](../../no-action.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close. Keep SKIP_HEXDOUBLE in p99-conformance.c, or change the comparison there to (0x1P2 > 3).
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The two lines of the ticket's `test.c` give error 66 for `has_hexdouble` on r17176. This was checked
for mcs51 with the small and large models and with `--std-c99` and `--std-c23`, and with `-c` for
stm8 and z80. The error is correct, because the second line declares an array of size 0.

## Reason

`0x1P2` is 4.0, so `(0x1P2 > 10)` is 0 and `has_hexdouble` is an array of 0 elements. The
constraint in C11 6.7.6.2 paragraph 1 says that an array size that is a constant expression has a
value greater than zero, and a conforming compiler issues a diagnostic when a constraint is
violated. SDCC gives the same error 66 for `double z[0];` and for the comparison written as
`(4.0 > 10)`.

GCC accepts arrays of size 0 as an extension, which explains why the P99 lines compile there.
GCC 14.2 with `-std=c11 -pedantic-errors` rejects both lines. Its first message says that the
enumerator value is not an integer constant expression, which follows from C11 6.6 paragraph 6.

SDCC evaluates hexadecimal floating constants correctly. A program compiled for mcs51 and run in
ucsim gave true for `0x1P2 == 4.0f`, 0 for `(0x1P2 > 10)`, and 12 for `(unsigned char) 0x1.8P3`.
`enum { e = (0x1P2 > 3) }; char a[e ? 1 : -1];` compiles for mcs51.

`support/regression/tests/p99-conformance.c` still defines `SKIP_HEXDOUBLE` with a reference to
this ticket. The ticket's comments say that it stays open only until that test is corrected.

## Related

A separate problem appeared during this check and has no ticket. On mcs51 an enumerator whose value
is a comparison of two equal constants, such as `enum { e = (4 == 4) };`, gives error 174
"enumeration constant not an integer". stm8 and z80 accept it. `enum { e = (0x1P2 == 4) };` fails
in this way on mcs51, so `(0x1P2 == 4)` is not a usable correction of the P99 lines.
